npcs.name: Eithne
npcs.idle: He doesn't cry like my baby. He doesn't smell like my baby. He's not my baby.

npcs.name: Wise-Woman Brid
npcs.idle: Brew water in an eggshell in front of a changeling and it'll speak. Ask me how I know.

npcs.name: Fergal the Fisher
npcs.idle: Seven years she was my wife. Seven good years.

npcs.name: Aoibhe
npcs.idle: Mam's coming back. She said she would. She said.

npcs.name: Mandra
npcs.idle: Sixteen, and he thinks he knows the world. I was sixteen once. I know exactly what he knows.

npcs.name: Bonesetter Nessa
npcs.idle: Bites, breaks and bad luck. Mostly bites, this season.

npcs.name: Farmer Cormac
npcs.idle: Turnips. A whole field. Dug up, bitten once each, and dropped.

npcs.name: Rhian the Dyer
npcs.idle: Woad for blue, weld for yellow, madder for red. And for pests - well. You'll see.

npcs.name: Orlaith the Herbwife
npcs.idle: Glowcaps, dew, mere-weed. Everything worth having grows where the good folk are.

npcs.name: Sabha
npcs.idle: Sabha watches the water. Sabha likes fish.

npcs.name: Tavie
npcs.idle: A drum's a heart you can hold. Mine was stolen.

npcs.name: Reeve Cathbad
npcs.idle: Every sack counted in. Every sack counted out. And still the numbers lie.

npcs.name: Fereinn
npcs.idle: Siabra, yes. Not theirs. Not anyone's. Say what you came to say.

npcs.name: Seanchai Oran
npcs.idle: Every barrow has a story. That one's story was 'stay shut'.

npcs.name: Riona
npcs.idle: A month in a siabra pit. Ask me how I am. Go on.

npcs.name: Ronan of the Roane
npcs.idle: The lake remembers everything. Lately it remembers blood.

npcs.name: Cara the Lorewoman
npcs.idle: Ask me about anything older than your grandmother. Newer things, ask the market.

npcs.name: Captain Lir
npcs.idle: Mag Mell has walls on three sides. The fourth side is the lake. Think about that.

quests.title: The Changeling
quests.offer:
My son was taken. I know how that sounds. He's in his cradle right now, and he's not him. He's thin, and he's old in the eyes, and he never stops crying, and he never stops eating.

Wise-Woman [Brid] says it's a changeling - that the good folk took my Cian and left one of theirs. Will you [find Cian]? Please. Everyone else thinks I'm mad.

topics.Brid: Brid lives by the well. She's delivered every baby in this town for forty years. She knows.

quests.summary: Eithne believes her baby son was taken by the good folk and a changeling left in his cradle.

steps.say: She's not mad. I brewed water in an eggshell by the cradle and the thing in it sat up and said 'I'm three hundred years old, and I've never seen that.' That's a changeling. Her Cian will be with the blackthorn folk, south of town, where the [fairy fort] is.

steps.goal: Go to the blackthorn fairy fort in the south
steps.text: A ring of blackthorn so thick no light gets through. Pale things move inside it, singing.

steps.goal: Get past the lunantishee who guard the fort
steps.text: They don't die - they wither into thorns. The singing stops. Somewhere inside, a baby starts to cry - a human cry.
The warden collapses into a heap of black twigs. Behind it, a cradle of woven thorn, and a fat pink baby kicking his legs.

stages.name: the Blackthorn Warden
stages.announce: The thorns heave and stand up into a tall, twisted shape. 'The child stays.'

steps.say:
Don't take him. Not yet. Please.

The one in his cradle is MINE. My son. He was born sick - faerie children sometimes are. Only a human mother's milk can save them. Three months at your breast and he'd live. I took hers so mine could have her. I'm sorry. I'm not sorry. I'd do it again. Ask her - will she [nurse him]?

CIAN. Oh - oh, my love, my lamb -

...She said that? That the other one will die? Without me?

I could [swap them back] tonight. Cian's home, and theirs goes back to the fort, and I never think about it again. Or I could [nurse both], until spring, and then give theirs back to her healthy. I have two arms. I don't know if I have the heart.

options.say: Tonight, then. I'll leave him at the thorns at dusk. ...I'll not think about it. I'll not.
Both. Until spring. Gods help me, he's ugly and he bites. ...Tell her. Tell her I'll keep him safe.

swapped.text: Take this. Brid says it's lucky.

both.text: Take this. The faerie mother left it on my step for you, this morning.

quests.title: The Roane Wife
quests.offer:
My wife Muirne was a roane - a seal-woman. Seven years ago I found her skin on the rocks and hid it, and she stayed, and married me, and we had a girl. I told myself she was happy.

A month ago she found the skin in the thatch and went back to the sea. And now Aoibhe says the roane on the north-east shore are being hunted for their skins. Will you [find Muirne]? Aoibhe knows where the [chest] was.

topics.chest: Ask Aoibhe. She's by the nets. She found it first.

quests.summary: Fergal hid his selkie wife's skin to keep her. She found it and went back to the sea - and now the roane are being hunted.

steps.say: Mam's skin was in the chest. In the thatch, in a chest. She found it when the roof leaked. She cried and cried and then she kissed me and went down to the water and didn't come back. Are you going to find her? Tell her the roof's [fixed].

steps.goal: Go to the north-east shore where the roane gather
steps.text: Seals in the shallows - and too many empty, bloody rocks. Something's been hunting here.
One carries a sack of sealskins. Not Muirne's. They mention 'the big one, the grey-and-silver' - taken alive to their master.
A dozen sealskins, salted and stacked. None of them grey-and-silver. A woman's voice, behind the tents, singing in a language like waves.
The skinner falls on his own knives. Behind him, a woman with her arms bound, and a grey-and-silver skin across his saddle.

stages.name: Maol the Skinner
stages.announce: A dergan in an apron of sealskin. 'The grey one's worth twenty. She's mine.'

steps.say:
Fergal sent you? ...Of course. He's a kind man. He was always a kind man, except for the once.

I loved him, you know. That's the cruel part. I loved him and I loved the sea, and he only gave me the choice of one. Is Aoibhe well? Is the roof [fixed]?

I could [go home] - with my skin in my own keeping this time, and stay because I choose to. Fergal will have to live with knowing I might leave.

Or I take Aoibhe [into the sea]. She's half roane. She'd learn the water in a summer. Fergal would have the house, and the boat, and the empty bed. Tell me. I've only ever been told.

options.say: Home. With my skin under my own pillow. ...He'll learn. We both will.
Then I'll come for her at the next tide. Tell him gently. Tell him she'll wave from the rocks.

steps.say:
She's home. She walked in with her skin over her arm and hung it on the peg by the door, where I can see it every day.

She says that's the bargain. I'd make it a thousand times.

She came at the tide and took Aoibhe. I watched from the door. Aoibhe waved.

She'll wave from the rocks, Muirne said. I'll be on the rocks every morning. Take this. It's from the boat. I won't fish again.

home.text: Take this. Muirne says it was meant for a friend of the roane.

quests.title: Youth Gone Wrong
quests.offer:
Oh - you're not one of them. Good. I've no time to talk. Two of the villainous youths came by the hall last night and said they'd be back for my son's [debts]. They said it like a promise.

Will you [stand with me]? Just tonight. Just till they've gone.

topics.debts: Dallan took their silver and wore their colours. Now they say he owes them, and if he won't pay, I will.

quests.summary: Mandra's son Dallan has run off with the villainous youths, and the gang has come to collect his debts from her.

steps.goal: Stand with Mandra behind the hall
steps.text: The last of them runs for the trees, shouting that Dallan will hear of this. Mandra sits down hard on the step.

stages.name: Keep Mandra safe
stages.announce: Two figures in gang colours step out from behind the hall, then two more. 'Where's the money, Mandra?'
stages.thanks: Thank you. Thank you. They'll not come back tonight.

stages.name: Scab
stages.announce: A big lad with a scabbed lip shoves through. 'Dallan's MY mate. His debts are MY debts.'

steps.say:
They called him one of theirs. My Dallan. He's sixteen, and soft, and he cries at lambing.

They camp in the woods west of the north road. Go and [look] for him. Don't hurt him. Please - whatever he's done, don't hurt him.

steps.goal: Find the villainous youths' north camp
steps.text: Ragged tents, a fire, a dog. And a boy's blue coat with a mended elbow hung on a branch. Dallan is here, or was.

steps.goal: Search Dallan's corner of the camp
steps.text: Under the bedroll, a purse of new silver - more than a boy earns robbing the road in a year. Every coin is stamped with a red hand.

steps.say:
Red hands. I've never seen coin like it.

He's alive. He's eating, by the weight of this. ...He's being paid, isn't he? Somebody's paying children to rob the road. Who does that? Who would ever pay for that?

default.text: Take this. It's not much. You stood behind my hall in the dark for a stranger.

quests.title: Mandra's Boy
quests.offer:
I asked the guards about the red hand. Nobody knows it, or nobody will say.

But Dallan will. Go back to the north camp and [talk to him]. Talk, not fight. If the lieutenant's about, he won't say a word, so thin the camp out first.
quests.summary: Dallan is being paid in red-hand silver. Mandra wants to know why - and by whom.

steps.goal: Thin out the recruits at the north camp
steps.text: With the recruits scattered, a boy in a blue coat slips away from the fire and waves you into the trees.

steps.say:
You came from Mam. I know. She sends everyone.

I'm not a fool. I know what they are. But listen: the lieutenant gets a purse every week from a man who doesn't talk like us. He talks like the folk across the lake. Red hand on the purse, red hand on his ring. He wants the road kept dangerous. Who'd [pay] for that?

If I go home now, they'll know I talked, and they'll come for Mam again. If I stay inside, I can find out who the man with the ring is.

Tell me. Do I [come home], or do I [stay inside]?

options.say: ...Home, then. Tell her I'm coming. Tell her to hide the good bread.
Right. I'll leave a white pebble on her gatepost every night I'm safe. Tell her to look.

steps.say:
He walked in an hour ago, ate everything in the house and fell asleep at the table.

He says there's a man with a red ring. He says it like it frightens him. It frightens me.

He's staying. With them. To spy, he says, like a boy in a story.

There was a white pebble on the gatepost this morning. I put it in my pocket. I'll keep every one.

home.text: He brought this home in his pocket. He wants you to have it.

inside.text: Take this. For watching over him.

quests.title: The Paymaster
quests.offer:
Dallan's sent word. The paymaster comes tonight to the east camp, the one on the hill above the north road. Dallan says he'll be there, at the fire, with the lieutenant's hand on his shoulder.

Catch the man with the red ring and we'll know who's buying our road. Will you [go to the east camp]?
quests.summary: The man who pays the villainous youths in red-hand silver comes tonight to their east camp.

steps.goal: Go to the villainous youths' east camp
steps.text: The lieutenant's fire. A horse that isn't a Hibernian horse, tied in the trees. Dallan by the fire, pale, and the lieutenant's hand heavy on his shoulder.
Corr goes down hard. The horse in the trees is gone - the paymaster rode off the moment the swords came out. Something fell from his saddle.

stages.name: Lieutenant Corr
stages.announce: 'You brought a friend, Dallan? You brought a FRIEND?'

steps.goal: Search where the paymaster's horse stood
steps.text: Orders, in a careful hand: 'Keep the north road bloody until the harvest is in. Keep the youths angry and paid. - R.' Sealed with a red hand.

steps.say:
'Keep the road bloody until the harvest is in.'

What happens after the harvest? ...Dallan's safe, at least. He ran all the way home. I'll show these to Reeve Cathbad; he counts everything, he'll know who counts in red hands.

default.text: Take this, with my thanks. And his.

quests.title: Breaking the Gang
quests.offer:
Without Corr, the youths in the north are lost lambs. Half have gone home already.

The south camp is different. The ringleader there is a grown man, and cruel, and Dallan says the red-hand silver goes through him first. Break him and the gang breaks. Take friends. Will you [break the gang]?
quests.summary: The rowdy ringleader at the south camp holds the villainous youths together - and handles the red-hand silver.

steps.goal: Fight through the rowdies at the south camp

steps.text: The ringleader falls. The camp melts into the woods - and from the high road north comes shouting: the highwaymen who took his silver are out on the road.

steps.say:
Dallan's home for good. He says the youths are going home too, in ones and twos - the ones with homes. The rest went to Mog, on the high road.

You gave me back my son. I can't give you anything like that. Take this.

default.text: And Dallan says to watch the high road. Mog's lot will be desperate now.

quests.title: Balm Hunt
quests.offer:
Cormac's boy came in with a bite on his leg the size of my hand. Rat boy, he says, up by the spring. It's gone angry.

I can draw it with a balm, but I need two things I don't keep: [mud] from a mudman, and a rat boy's tail. Will you [fetch them]?

topics.mud: Mudman mud has a bit of the curmudgeons' magic in it. Draws poison like nothing else. They shamble round the store east of town.

quests.summary: Farmer Cormac's son was bitten by rat boys at the spring. Bonesetter Nessa needs the makings of a balm.

steps.goal: Take a tail from a rat boy at the hideout
steps.text: A tail. A sorry thing. Nessa said any one would do.

steps.goal: Scrape mud from a mudman by the curmudgeons' store
steps.text: The mudman slumps into a heap that's mostly mud. You take a handful. It's warm, and it twitches.

steps.say:
Good. Hold his leg. ...There. The swelling's going already.

Tadhg says it wasn't just rat boys at the spring. The spraggons and the lucradans were there too, all three at each other's throats. Over water, he says. Tell his father.

default.text: Take this. And wash your hands before you eat anything.

quests.title: Three Kinds of Trouble
quests.offer:
My fields are ruined. Not robbed - ruined. Dug, trampled, every turnip bitten once and dropped.

Nessa says the pests are fighting up at the spring, and I say they're fighting through my field to get there. Rhian the dyer has an idea about [marking] them. Daft, but I've none better. Will you [help Rhian]?

topics.marking: She wants to dye them. The raiders. So we know which of them comes down the hill at night. I said daft.

quests.summary: Something crosses Cormac's fields every night. Rhian the dyer means to find out what, with dye.

steps.say:
Cormac thinks I'm daft. I'm not. Wild lucradans moult in autumn - hair everywhere. Spraggonolls carry bone charms. Rat boys, well, rat boys I can find by the smell.

Bring me lucradan hair and a spraggon charm and I'll brew a [dye] that clings to whatever made it. Splash the furrows, and in the morning we'll see whose feet are what colour.

steps.goal: Gather hair from wild lucradans at the warren
Take a bone charm from a spraggonoll at the den

steps.say: There. Three pots: blue for the lucradans, yellow for the spraggons, red for the rat boys. Off you go - splash Cormac's [furrows] and leave it a while.

steps.goal: Splash the furrows in Cormac's field
steps.text: By the time you come back, the field is a mess of colour: blue prints, yellow prints, red prints - all of them heading not into the field but through it, north, towards the spring. And over the lot, the broad flat prints of something heavy that took no dye at all. It came from the east.

steps.say:
They're not raiding me. They're crossing me - all three, going for the spring.

And something else coming from the east after them. Something with flat feet. I don't like the sound of that at all.

default.text: Take this, from Rhian and me. Proof that the daft idea worked.

quests.title: The Spring Runs Dry
quests.offer:
I walked up to the spring this morning. It's a trickle. Forty years it's run full, and now it's a trickle. No wonder they're killing each other for it.

Springs don't stop. Somebody's stopped it. Will you [find out who]?
quests.summary: The hill spring north of Mag Mell has nearly run dry, and the three pest tribes are at war over what's left.

steps.goal: Go to the spring in the hills
steps.text: The basin is half dry, the mud around it churned by a hundred small feet. And a new ditch, neatly dug, leading east from the rock.
A curmudgeon-made spade, left in the ditch. Its handle is carved with a little round scowling face: the mark of Grogan's people.
The ditch runs east under the hill, straight to the curmudgeons' store - where a dam of packed mud holds the stolen water in a pond for their mill wheel. Flat-footed mudmen splash along its top.
Clabber tumbles off his dam. One good kick and the mud gives way; the water rushes back down the ditch towards the spring.

stages.name: Clabber the Ditch-Digger
stages.announce: A curmudgeon in a mud-caked apron stands up on the dam. 'MY water! Dug it MYSELF!'

steps.say:
The spring's running! I heard it from the house.

And the pests are still up there, all three, and no less angry for it. They've had a taste of war now. I could [leave them be] - they'll settle, once there's water enough. Or the lads and I could [drive them off] the hill while they're tired.

options.say: Leave them be. ...Aye. They were here before the turnips.
Then I'll tell the lads. Keep your head down - you'll hear it from the house.

peace.text: Take this. And thank you for the water. I never thought to say that to anyone.

war.text: Take this. And stay clear of the spring for a while - or don't, if you like a fight.

quests.title: Grubb's Truce
quests.offer:
There's a spraggon up there calls himself Grubb Bigfist. King of the hill, he says, and now the spring's running he won't let the others near it.

The rat boys and the lucradans would go home if he let them drink. Will you [deal with Grubb]?
quests.summary: Grubb Bigfist the spraggon holds the spring and won't share it, and the hill war goes on.

steps.text: Grubb's spraggons hold the spring. The rat boys and lucradans watch from the rocks, thirsty and furious.
Grubb sits down in the spring with a splash and bursts into tears. The rat boys and lucradans creep down to drink, warily, and nobody bites anybody.

steps.say:
Quiet up there tonight. First quiet night since spring.

That ditch-spade's hanging over my door now. A reminder: when the little folk fight, look for who's stealing their water. Clabber said a man paid him for the mill. A man with a red ring.

default.text: Take this, with the thanks of every turnip I'll ever grow.

quests.title: Dew from the Mere
quests.offer:
Ailbhe gathers my glowcaps; that's the easy work. What I need now is dew from the mere in the west - the fae lake - gathered off the lily-pads before the sun's on them.

It's the best thing there is for a fever, and the good folk guard it like gold. Will you [gather the dew]?
quests.summary: Orlaith the herbwife needs dew from the fae mere, and the fae don't share.

steps.goal: Go to the mere in the west
steps.text: Still water, white lilies, and a silence that feels like being watched. Out on the mere, tall pale shapes stand knee-deep, guarding something.
You fill the phial drop by drop. The watching shapes turn your way, all at once.
The last sprite bursts into a shower of petals. Out on the water a woman's voice says, very clearly: 'Thief.'

steps.say:
'Thief.' She said that? ...Ach.

They always want paying. That's the trouble with the good folk: they never give, they only lend, and the interest is murder.

default.text: Take this - and don't go back to the mere alone for a while.

quests.title: Balance of Nature
quests.offer:
There's a creature lives by the mere - Sabha, the fishers call it. Harmless. A go-between, my mother said.

If the Lady wants paying, Sabha will know the price. Take it a [fish] - it likes fish - and ask. Will you [speak to Sabha]?

topics.fish: Fresh, mind. From the shore, not the market. Sabha can tell.

quests.summary: The Lady of the Mere calls you a thief. Sabha, the go-between by the mere, will know her price.

steps.goal: Find a fish on the mere shore
steps.text: One fat trout, still kicking. You leave a coin in the trap. It seems only fair, given the day you're having.

steps.say:
Fish. Good fish. Sabha says thank you.

The Lady is angry. Her dew was taken. Price is music. The Lady has not heard music since the [drum] of Tir na mBeo stopped playing at the water. Drum is stolen. Bring the drum, play the drum - Lady forgives.

Music. Of course it's music.

Tavie of Tir na mBeo used to drum by the mere every midsummer, and the fae came out of the lilies to listen. Her drum went missing in the spring. Go and see her - she's in Tir na mBeo, by the inn.

default.text: Take this, for your trouble with the fish.

quests.title: Beautiful Music
quests.offer:
My drum! My beautiful drum. Sprites took it - little red angry things, [anger sprites], came in the window, took it and laughed.

I've heard it since, out east of the fae woods, somebody beating it badly. Will you [find my drum]?

topics.anger sprites: Born of a bad temper, my granny said. They gather wherever someone's been cruel - lately that's the east, by the Dergan camps.

quests.summary: Tavie's drum was stolen by anger sprites. The Lady of the Mere wants to hear it played again.

steps.text: One of them drops what it was beating on: a goatskin drum, split clean across.

steps.say:
Split. They've split it. ...It'll mend. It needs a new head.

Curmudgeon-cured hide is the best there is, I hate to say. Their trappers cure it with something that stinks for a month and lasts a hundred years. Bring me a [hide].

steps.goal: Take a cured hide from a curmudgeon trapper in the east valley

steps.say:
There. Listen to that! ...Now, the Lady.

I'll play at the mere, but I'll not go alone. The fae in the west aren't what they were. Meet me by the [water].

steps.goal: Keep Tavie safe while she plays
steps.text: The drumming rolls out over the water. One by one the sprites stop and sit down in the reeds to listen. Out on the mere, a tall pale woman stands up from the lilies.

stages.name: Keep Tavie safe
stages.announce: Tavie sits on a stone and starts to play. The water shivers, and the sprites come in a rush.
stages.thanks: Did you hear it? Did you hear how the water answered?

steps.goal: Speak with the Lady of the Mere
steps.say:
Twenty summers without the drum.

You took my dew, and you brought me music. The debt is paid. Tell your herbwife the mere is not her garden. She may take what she is [given]. No more.

She smiled at me. The Lady of the Mere smiled at ME.

I'll play every midsummer now till I'm dead. Take this - for the hide, and the walk, and the company.

default.text: Take this. Something to remember the music by.

quests.title: The Lady's Bargain
quests.offer:
'Only what she's given.' Hah.

A fever went through Tir na mBeo last week, and do you know how much dew she's given me? None. Children are sick and she sits on her lilies.

I need that dew. How you get it is up to you. Will you [get the dew]?
quests.summary: A fever in Tir na mBeo, and only the mere's dew will cure it. The Lady of the Mere won't give it.

steps.goal: Decide how to get the dew
steps.say: So. Do you [take it] - with friends at your back, past her guardians and her - or do you go and [ask the Lady], and see what she wants this time?

options.say: Then take friends. She's older than this town, and she won't go quietly.
Ask, then. Mind she doesn't ask for your name.

steps.goal: Defeat the Lady of the Mere
steps.text: The Lady sinks into the mere without a sound, and the lilies close over her. The dew is yours. Nothing on the water moves.

steps.say:
Enough for every child in Tir na mBeo, and to spare.

...It's very quiet out at the mere now, Ailbhe says. No singing at all. I suppose that's the price. I suppose I'll get used to it.

steps.goal: Ask the Lady of the Mere
steps.say:
Sick children. ...I am not cruel. I am old, and I have been robbed.

Very well. Dew for the sick, every season, for as long as the herbwife plants foxglove and meadowsweet on my shore, for the bees. A [bargain].

Foxglove and meadowsweet. For the bees.

That's all she wanted? A garden for the bees? Twenty years I've been stealing from her. ...Here. And send me your fevers, any time.

took.text: Take this. It's yours, I suppose. All of it's yours.

asked.text: Take this. The Lady left it on my doorstep. With a bee on it.

quests.title: Short Measures
quests.offer:
Forty sacks of barley in that granary at harvest. Thirty-one now. No door forced, no lock broken.

Guardian Fionn says curmudgeons. I say curmudgeons can't walk through walls. Will you [look into it]?
quests.summary: Barley is vanishing from Mag Mell's granary without a lock broken. Reeve Cathbad wants to know how.

steps.text: Under the last row of sacks, a hole - not dug from inside, but from below. The earth around it is wet clay, and it smells of the marsh.
The clay trail ends at the curmudgeons' store. Harvesters are packing barley sacks into carts - Mag Mell's sacks, with the reeve's own mark on them.
A board of notches: sacks in, sacks out. The 'out' notches are marked with a little red hand.

steps.say:
Tunnels. Mudmen dig through clay like it's water.

And a red hand on the tally. Mandra's lad talked about a red hand. I'm starting to think someone's buying our harvest and our troubles both.

default.text: Take this. You've a reeve's eye for a short measure.

quests.title: The Watch's New Armour
quests.offer:
I'm putting a watch on the next cart, and the watch needs armour. Kylirean the armourer will stitch it if he has the [makings] - and he's fussy.

Bring him the makings, then ride with the cart. Will you [outfit the watch]?

topics.makings: Lough wolf skins for the jerkins. Mudman chert for the studs - there's good flint in them, if you break them right.

quests.summary: Reeve Cathbad's watch will guard the next grain cart, once Kylirean the armourer has the makings of their armour.

steps.goal: Take skins from lough wolves in the northern hills
Break chert from mudmen by the curmudgeons' store

steps.say:
Kylirean grumbled and sewed all night, and the watch looks like a watch now.

The cart goes out by the old mill road. Meet it at the [mill].

steps.goal: Guard the grain cart on the mill road
steps.text: Tharl drops with a curse. In his belt pouch: a note in siabra script, and a wax seal - a red hand.

stages.name: Keep the grain cart safe
stages.announce: Curmudgeons boil up out of the ditches on both sides of the road. 'GRAIN!'
stages.thanks: The carter wipes his face. 'Never again. Never, ever again.'

stages.name: Tharl the Trapper
stages.announce: A curmudgeon with a trap-chain over his shoulder steps out of the hedge. 'That's MY cart. Paid for.'

steps.say:
Siabra script. I can't read it. Nobody in Mag Mell can.

There's a siabra exile on the east shore who sells what he knows, they say in Tir na mBeo. A siabra. Gods help us.

default.text: Take this. Kylirean made one extra. For the watch's best.

quests.title: The Lesser of Two Evils
quests.offer:
Fereinn, the exile is called. He lives alone on the east shore, hated by both sides, which I suppose recommends him.

Take him Tharl's note. Will you [find Fereinn]?
quests.summary: A siabra exile on the east shore can read Tharl's note - for a price.

steps.goal: Find Fereinn on the east shore
steps.say:
Tharl's hand. Dergan wax.

I'll read it. Not for coin - for a courtesy. A curmudgeon courier carries the next note of this kind today, on the shore road. Bring me his [plans], and I'll read you both.

steps.goal: Stop the curmudgeon courier on the shore road
steps.text: The courier squeals and drops a satchel.

steps.say:
Here is what they say. The curmudgeons sell your barley to the Dergan war camp. The camp feeds an army for the island. The one who pays is the warlord's quartermaster, and he signs with a red hand.

Now. I could [keep the plans] - they're worth a great deal to the siabra who hate the warlord, my own people, and you'd have my friendship. Or you [take them] to your reeve, and I've done you a kindness for nothing. Choose.

options.say: Then you have a friend on the east shore. Few can say that. None of them are siabra.
As you like. Kindness is a habit I'm trying to keep.

steps.say:
You gave them to a siabra?

...Well. He told you the truth, which is more than the curmudgeons ever did. The enemy of my enemy. I'll sleep badly.

The warlord's quartermaster. Feeding an army on Mag Mell barley.

I'll take this to Guardian Fionn tonight. You've done Mag Mell a great service.

siabra.text: Take this anyway. You found the truth, whoever has the paper.

reeve.text: Take this. It opens doors at any granary in the realm.

quests.title: Hughar's Ledger
quests.offer:
The curmudgeons' go-between is Hughar the poacher - the one with the cruiach daemon hide that Alastriona swears was hers.

He keeps the ledger: every sack, every coin, every red hand. Bring me that ledger and Guardian Fionn can take it to the High King. Take friends. Hughar's no fool. Will you [take the ledger]?
quests.summary: Hughar the poacher keeps the curmudgeons' ledger of every sack sold across the lake.

steps.goal: Fight through the poachers in the east valley

steps.text: Hughar goes down hard. In his pack: a fat ledger, a stolen cruiach daemon hide, and a purse of red-hand silver.

steps.say:
Every sack. Every coin. Three seasons of it, and all of it going across the lake to the Dergans.

They're not raiding us. They're provisioning. You don't provision for a raid. You provision for a war.

default.text: Take this. And this - Alastriona says the hide is yours now.

quests.title: Bones on the Road
quests.offer:
Skeletons on the north road at night. The roadwardens have lost two good men to them.

Now - the dead in that barrow have lain quiet for three hundred years. The dead don't [wake] on their own. Will you [go to the barrow]?

topics.wake: Not by themselves. Someone has to call them, or let them out. That's the old law, and the old law's never been wrong yet.

quests.summary: The dead of the old barrow by Mag Mell walk the roads at night. Seanchai Oran says the dead don't wake on their own.

steps.goal: Put down the skeletal pawns at the barrow

steps.text: The great stone over the barrow door has been cracked - not by frost, not by age. Chisel marks, fresh ones. And pressed into the clay round the crack, the mark of a ring: a hand.

give.name: a clay print of a ring

steps.say:
Someone opened it. On purpose.

The Parthanan farm folk saw lights in the Grey Wood before the bones came. Rest tonight. Tomorrow we look there.

default.text: Take this. Old things for an old business.

quests.title: Lights in the Grey Wood
quests.offer:
The Parthanan farmers say there were lights in the haunted wood - red ones - and singing that wasn't siabra singing.

Go and [look]. By day, if you've any sense. The Grey Wood's bad enough by daylight.
quests.summary: Red lights and strange singing in the haunted Grey Wood came before the dead walked.

steps.goal: Go to the edge of the haunted wood
steps.text: Grey trees, grey moss, and a mist that never quite lifts. On the stumps: candle-ends of red wax, dozens of them, in a ring.
Red wax, stamped with the same hand. And a scrap of paper: 'Every night you sing, the dead walk further. Sing until they reach Mag Mell.'
The wraiths come apart like cobweb. Behind them, in the mud, boot prints going south - towards the farm.

steps.goal: Follow the trail to the Parthanan farm road
steps.text: The farm road. Fresh hoofprints, and a farmhand who will not look you in the eye.
A letter in a careful hand: 'To the Summoner. Keep the barrow open until the harvest is in. Your fee waits at the outpost. - R.' The red hand again.

steps.say:
'Keep the barrow open until the harvest is in.' The same words as the gang's orders, Mandra says. The same R.

Someone wants Mag Mell busy - busy with bandits, busy with bones, busy with curmudgeons - until the harvest is in. And the Summoner will sing tonight. Listen.

default.text: Take this. And stay indoors after dark, unless you mean to do something about it.

quests.title: Riona's Revenge
quests.offer:
You're the one who found the letter? Then hear me.

The siabra at the outpost on the east shore took me and kept me a month in a pit. Their chieftain, Dergal, wears a vest of runes - and every night a man in a grey hood came, and Dergal paid him in red-hand silver. The Summoner.

I want Dergal dead, and I want that vest. Will you [take my revenge]?
quests.summary: Riona was held by the siabra at the Dergan outpost, where Chieftain Dergal paid the Summoner.

steps.goal: Cut through the siabra at the Dergan outpost

steps.text: Dergal falls. His runed vest smoulders; the runes match the marks on the barrow stone - binding runes, and unbinding.

stages.name: Chieftain Dergal
stages.announce: A siabra in a vest stitched with burning runes: 'The pit girl sent you? I should have kept her longer.'

steps.say:
Dead. Good.

Those are unbinding runes - the same that cracked your barrow. Dergal taught the Summoner, and paid him. And Dergal was paid by the island. ...Here. Wear it, if you can stand the smell.

default.text: Take it. It was always meant for someone who'd use it better than he did.

quests.title: The Summoner
quests.offer:
We know what he is now, and who pays him. The Summoner works at the barrow by night, singing the dead up.

Riona says he'll run when he hears his paymaster's dead - unless someone stops him first. Bring friends, go to the barrow, and [end it].
quests.summary: The Summoner sings the dead out of the old barrow by Mag Mell, in the pay of the island.

steps.text: The barrow door stands open. Inside, a man in a grey hood, singing, and the dead climbing up round him.
The Summoner falls. The song breaks off mid-note, and every skeleton in the barrow lies down at once, like tired men. On his hand, a heavy signet: a red hand on lake-blue enamel.

stages.name: the Summoner
stages.announce: The singing stops. 'The bones are mine. The road is mine. Mag Mell will be the warlord's.' The dead turn towards you.

steps.say:
A red hand on lake blue.

That's the seal of Clan Derg, the old warlords of the lake. I thought them a story. A warlord, with coin enough to buy bandits and curmudgeons and the dead? ...Take this to the roane. The lake's going red.

default.text: Take this. The barrow's quiet. That's your doing.

quests.title: What the Roane Saw
quests.offer:
Muirne says you're a friend of the roane. Then hear what the roane see from the water.

Boats cross to the island every night. Barley going over, men coming back. The Dergans are gathering under a warlord, and they hunt us because we see too much. Will you [learn what they are]? The lorewoman in Tir na mBeo knows the old stories.
quests.summary: The roane see boats crossing to Dergan Island every night. Cara the lorewoman knows the old stories of the Dergans.

steps.goal: Ask Cara the Lorewoman about the Dergans
steps.say:
Dergans. Siabra, of the unseelie court, that came through the Veil when the elves and lurikeens did, and never went home. Here they took the lake's name: Clan Derg, the red lake.

Their warlords cut their oaths on [war-stones] - uncut stones from the lake bed, carried by their furies. Bring me one and I'll read it for you.

steps.goal: Take a war-stone from a dergan fury

steps.say:
An oath-stone, cut with a warlord's name: Ruadhan. Ruadhan of the Red Hand.

...R. The letters signed 'R.' He's on the island, and he's sworn to take the lake shore 'when the harvest is in'. Tell the [roane].

steps.goal: Return to Ronan of the Roane
steps.say:
Ruadhan.

The roane will watch the war camp for you, from the water. Go when you're ready. And take this - from Muirne.

default.text: From Muirne, with the roane's thanks.

quests.title: Scouting the War Camp
quests.offer:
The war camp on the south shore is where Ruadhan's bands muster before they cross.

Get close. Count them. Find out when they march. Will you [scout the camp]?
quests.summary: Ruadhan's war bands muster at the Dergan war camp on the south shore.

steps.goal: Reach the high ground north of the war camp
steps.text: Below you: tents for a hundred, cookfires, siabra archers on the palisade - and Mag Mell's barley sacks piled under oilcloth.

steps.goal: Circle round to the camp's east side
steps.text: The training ground beyond is busy: recruits drilling in lines, sergeants shouting in the siabra tongue. More than a war band. An army.

steps.goal: Thin the furies guarding the war tent

steps.text: A muster roll: bands, numbers and a date, written in common so the curmudgeons can read it. 'Muster at the outpost. Cross when the harvest is in.' The harvest is in next week.

steps.say:
Next week.

Take it to the captain in Mag Mell. And thank you. The roane don't forget. ...Listen - the war bands are already moving on the east edge. They know someone was in the camp.

default.text: Take this. You've a roane's eyes now.

quests.title: Orders from the Outpost
quests.offer:
So the roane were right, and the reeve, and old Oran, and a boy from a bandit camp. Ruadhan's been buying our troubles for a year.

Before I can move the guard, I need his orders in his own hand. The outpost on the east shore carries them to the war bands. Will you [take the orders]?
quests.summary: Captain Lir needs Ruadhan's own orders before he can move the guard. The Dergan outpost carries them.

steps.goal: Silence the whistlers who watch the outpost road

steps.text: The quartermaster falls before the fire catches. In his satchel: Ruadhan's orders, sealed in red.

stages.name: Quartermaster Fiachna
stages.announce: A Dergan in a quartermaster's sash snatches up a satchel. 'Burn the orders! BURN them!'

steps.goal: Bring the orders to Captain Lir
steps.say:
'Hold the island against all comers. When the harvest is in, cross and take Mag Mell's granary, then the town.' Signed: Ruadhan, warlord of the Red Lake.

Well. Now I can move.

default.text: Take this, and the realm's thanks. You'll have more than that before we're done.

quests.title: The Roane Captives
quests.offer:
One thing more, before your captain sails.

Ruadhan keeps roane in pens on the island's south shore. Our skins are his treasury. If the island is stormed, the guards will kill them first. Will you [free the captives] before then? Take friends. The island is his.
quests.summary: Ruadhan keeps roane captive in pens on Dergan Island's south shore.

steps.goal: Reach the pens on the island's south shore
steps.text: Pens of driftwood and net, and grey shapes inside them that turn their heads to watch you. A sergeant shouts.

steps.goal: Free the roane and hold the pens
steps.text: The pens are open. Roane slip into the water one by one, grey heads in the waves, and the last of them turns and sings something you'll never forget.

stages.name: Keep the roane captives safe
stages.announce: You cut the first net. Every Dergan on the south shore comes running.
stages.thanks: The roane captive presses your hand, once, and is gone into the water.

stages.name: Slavemaster Cuan
stages.announce: A Dergan with a sealskin whip wades out of the shallows. 'My stock. MY treasury.'

steps.say:
Every one of them. Every one.

Ruadhan will know by morning. Tell your captain to be quick - and when the island is stormed, the roane will carry anyone who asks across the water. That's a promise.

default.text: Take this. The roane have long memories, and you're in all of them now.
